captain_dispatch_inputs.input: 1. No workspace identity anywhere in the settings path; the write-back target is a DECISION with a stated failure mode; no silent multi-root guess.
captain_dispatch_inputs.answer: DESIGN §A. Target set = the DISTINCT LIVE SESSION WORKSPACE ROOTS at event time via the adapter's existing dsh.workspaceRootsAll() (measured packages/mpd-dsh-adapter-plugin/src/index.ts:173,298,415). 0 roots: write no file, persist in settings, warn once, report writtenTo:[] with reason 'no-live-session', and tell the user to start a session in the intended workspace; 1 root: write it and say so; N roots: REFUSE with reason 'ambiguous-multi-root', name every candidate root, write no file, and tell the user how to make it unambiguous — this REVERSES the first draft's fan-out, because t35 acceptance A3 requires the ambiguous multi-root path to warn and never silently write to a guessed path (D-12). process.cwd() is never a fallback. 'Per-session attribution where the event carries it' is recorded as IMPOSSIBLE because both settings events are namespace-only; last-writer-wins and any single guessed root are rejected by name as the forbidden silent mis-targeting. User-visible wording is given for each of the three cases.

captain_dispatch_inputs.input: 2. No comment-preserving JSONC writer exists offline; the editor must REFUSE rather than corrupt; specify strings/escapes, comments, trailing commas, arrays, duplicate keys, missing key path, CRLF/LF, and a file changed between read and write.
captain_dispatch_inputs.answer: DESIGN §B. The writer is REFUSE-FIRST: surgicalEdit(rawText, path, value) returns {ok:true,text} only when the exact span is proven, else {ok:false,reason} with the file BYTE-UNTOUCHED, a loud warning, and the settings layer still taking effect (a config file destroyed by a UI save is the worst outcome). Editor = the repo's own scanner (packages/mpd-config-plugin/src/index.ts:22-48) extended into a path-addressed value-span rewriter; vendoring is the explicit fallback only. E1-E11 matrix: string/escape handling with decoded-key matching; comments before/inside objects and after the last member survive verbatim; trailing-comma style detected and matched and delete re-checks for ',,'; arrays supported including delete-to-empty; DUPLICATE KEYS edit the LAST occurrence (JSON.parse is last-wins, measured) and REFUSE on an ambiguous duplicated intermediate; a missing key path materialises intermediates and appends as the LAST member with no invented comment; CRLF/LF detected and preserved with new lines matching the dominant ending; a read/write race is handled by compare-and-swap with N=3 retries then 'conflict' leaving the human's file untouched; unparsable => no edit attempted; missing => created with a header comment; read-only => loud 'denied' with path+errno.

captain_dispatch_inputs.input: 3. The web write path has a trap: a NON-LOOPBACK page runs in memory persistence and never reaches the host document; exercise the card from a LOOPBACK page and state the honest evidence level when that cannot be witnessed (no browser here).
captain_dispatch_inputs.answer: DESIGN §C. The card must be exercised from a LOOPBACK page, and the card's own copy states that a remote page is effectively read-only. Evidence levels are split and labelled: W1 witnessable (the authenticated settings/mutate over the host HTTP API changes the namespace, the bridge runs, the file changes) proves the BRIDGE, which is this design's subject; W2 witnessable statically (the built client contains the settings.plugin.item registration for key 'mpd', asserted against shipped/served bytes); W3 NOT witnessable here (that the card renders, is dispatched for the mpd namespace, and a click produces the mutate) is explicitly NOT-CLAIMED with the reason recorded. The design therefore claims 'a loopback client's mutate persists', never 'the Web page always persists'.

captain_dispatch_inputs.input: 4. applies:'restart' — say which knobs take effect immediately and which genuinely need a restart, and what the TUI hints must say after the bridge.
captain_dispatch_inputs.answer: DESIGN §D. Measured per-knob: every knob the /settings section exposes is captured at apply() by its consumer (mpd-boulder-plugin:31,45; mpd-comment-checker-plugin:26,99; mpd-hashline-plugin:40; mpd-ulw-plugin:26; mpd-memory-plugin:24) => RESTART for hashline.maxDiffChars, commentChecker.autoCheck (+bin/timeout/maxMessageChars), ulw.maxRounds, memory.vcs, team.stateDir and boulder.dir. The ONE immediate family is extensions.*, read lazily per use by mpd-ext-plugin (src/manifest.ts:193-210, src/mcp.ts:50) and not exposed by the section. The config layer itself is immediate via mpd_config_get after mpd_config_reload (measured index.ts:104,134-141; its README claims no more). Post-bridge hints: the word 'not bridged' is DELETED, not softened, and replaced by a two-part statement naming the file written and the restart requirement, with a runtime notice for the no-live-session case; one constant + one helper remain single-sourced and the existing test/plugin.test.ts assertion is extended.

acceptance_evidence.criterion: A LAYER PRECEDENCE table states, for each of project .mpd/mpd.jsonc, user $DSH_HOME/mpd.jsonc and the settings namespace, which wins and why, and shows what a user sees after an edit in each front door when a key exists in more than one layer.
acceptance_evidence.where: DESIGN §1.1 (L0 schema defaults < L1 $DSH_HOME/mpd.jsonc < L2 <workspace>/.mpd/mpd.jsonc < L3 settings user; L3 wins at runtime, L2 is the durable home) and §1.2 (a four-step worked trace of a UI edit over an existing file key, including the L3>L2 trap and the rule that a file edit CLEARS the overlapping override via the provider's unset/reset path). §1.3 records the measured installSection constraint with D-8 and the fallback.

acceptance_evidence.criterion: The WRITE-BACK design names the owning module, the exact trigger (which host event/call), the write path, atomicity/partial-write handling, and what happens when the target file is read-only, missing, or being edited concurrently by the user.
acceptance_evidence.where: DESIGN §2 (owner mpd-config-plugin, D-3; trigger settings/document-updated filtered to source==='update', D-4, with settings/updated secondary; the ordered sequence at §2.2), §B.3 (lock + compare-and-swap + sibling temp + atomic rename; multi-file writes explicitly not transactional, reported per root), and §B.2 E8/E9/E10/E11 (concurrent => retry x3 then 'conflict' leaving the human's file untouched; unparsable => no edit attempted; missing => created with a header comment; read-only => loud 'denied' with path + errno while the settings edit still succeeds).

acceptance_evidence.criterion: The WORKSPACE-SELECTION rule is stated for zero, one and several live session roots, with the failure mode of each and the loud degradation when the target is ambiguous (never a silent best-guess).
acceptance_evidence.where: DESIGN §A.1 — a three-row table giving the target, the failure mode and the exact USER-VISIBLE message for 0 / 1 / N live roots: 1 root writes it, 0 roots persist to settings and warn 'no-live-session', and N roots REFUSE with 'ambiguous-multi-root' naming every candidate and writing nothing (the fan-out of the first draft is REVERSED, D-12, to satisfy t35 acceptance A3's 'never silently write to a guessed path'). The target set is read from the adapter's workspaceRootsAll() because the settings events carry no identity (DOSSIER §c). Explicitly rejected: per-session attribution (impossible), last-writer-wins, and any single guessed root. process.cwd() is never a fallback. §A.1 also records the later-started-session behaviour and marks workspaceRootsAll()'s dedup/deleted-cwd behaviour UNVERIFIED for the lane to pin.

acceptance_evidence.criterion: The COMMENT-PRESERVATION strategy is specified: which editor/parser performs the edit, how key order and comments survive, and what happens for a key path that does not exist yet.
acceptance_evidence.where: DESIGN §B. Refuse-first result contract; editor = the in-repo string-aware scanner at packages/mpd-config-plugin/src/index.ts:22-48 extended into a path-addressed value-span rewriter (D-6); byte-identical elsewhere by construction because only the target span is spliced. Missing key path = E6 (materialise intermediates at the deepest existing point, append as the LAST member, no invented comment; D-7 rejects alphabetical insert because it reorders a human's file). Every case the captain named is a numbered row: E1 strings/escapes, E2 comments, E3 trailing commas, E4 arrays, E5 duplicate keys, E7 CRLF/LF, E8 read/write race, E9 unparsable, E10 missing, E11 read-only.

acceptance_evidence.criterion: The INVARIANTS section states how the design keeps: (1) mpd-tui-plugin performing ZERO filesystem writes, (2) mpd-dsh-adapter-plugin as the only contact surface with harness services, (3) mpd-config-plugin as the owner of the config layer, (4) no new filesystem write from any web/client code.
acceptance_evidence.where: DESIGN §5, one row per invariant. (1) the bridge lives in mpd-config-plugin and the TUI change is a STRING CONSTANT only; measured today the package imports only readFileSync/readdirSync/statSync (src/state.ts:11, src/registration.ts:17) with no write API in src/ or dist/, and U16 asserts it stays so. (2) ctx.settings is reached only through a NEW adapter seam, never a bare ctx.get('settings'). (3) mpd-config-plugin owns registration, both file layers, precedence and per-call root resolution (never a cached const, never chdir). (4) the card writes via settingsScope.mutate so the write rides the settings/mutate RPC and no client-side filesystem write exists.

acceptance_evidence.criterion: A FAILURE-MODES AND DISCLOSURES list says exactly what the docs must then disclose (including anything the bridge still cannot do), so the documentation task can be honest without inventing.
acceptance_evidence.where: DESIGN §7, eight numbered disclosures: no-live-session => no file write with the user-visible wording, non-loopback pages never reach the host document (memory mode), N-workspace fan-out, applies:'restart' with the per-knob table reference, file-edit-clears-override, inserted keys carry no comment, refuse-first outcomes leaving the file byte-untouched while the settings value still applies, and an explicit still-not-bridged list to be enumerated by name. §7 also requires items 1-4 and 7 to be visible in the product surface, not only the docs, and §C.3 forces the rendered web card to be recorded NOT-CLAIMED.

acceptance_evidence.criterion: A TEST PLAN names the unit tests and the two live lanes (TUI edit -> file changed -> plugin behaviour changed; web card edit -> same) that would falsify the design if wrong, with the exact commands where they exist.
acceptance_evidence.where: DESIGN §9. Unit tests U1-U17, one per edge case and invariant (byte fidelity, escapes, nested missing path, delete, arrays, duplicate keys including the ambiguous-intermediate refusal, CRLF, compare-and-swap, unparsable, read-only, missing, precedence both directions, no-workspace-identity, fan-out, migration idempotence, TUI zero-write, restart timing). Two live lanes with concrete commands: `node skills/dsh-qa/scripts/tui-settings-bridge.mjs` (tmux, real TTY, excluded from the automated sweep exactly like the existing TUI lanes) and `node skills/dsh-qa/scripts/web-settings-bridge.mjs` (loopback 303 + launch-token cookie, then the same settings/mutate the card emits, plus the static client-bundle assertion). Each asserts all three of accepted / file-changed-with-comments-intact / consumer-behaviour-changed-after-restart, on its own lane-root sandbox. §9.3 lists falsifiers F1-F9 and rules that a lane asserting only 'the edit was accepted' is not a pass.

decisions_recorded.decision: runtime precedence L0 < L1 < L2 < L3 (settings user wins at runtime)
decisions_recorded.rationale: a UI edit must be visible immediately; making the file outrank the settings layer is the bug being fixed.

decisions_recorded.decision: a file edit CLEARS the overlapping settings override via unset
decisions_recorded.rationale: otherwise L3 > L2 silently swallows every later file edit (the trap traced in §1.2).
the only module owning both file layers, the JSONC reader, deepMerge and the workspace helper; keeps the TUI zero-write property.

decisions_recorded.decision: trigger is settings/document-updated filtered to source==='update'
decisions_recorded.rationale: document-updated fires on raw-section change regardless of the deep-equal gate; the source filter prevents a write-back/reload echo loop.

decisions_recorded.decision: target set = live roots at event time; write all N; [] => persist + warn, never guess
decisions_recorded.rationale: the settings path carries no workspace identity (DOSSIER §c), and silent mis-targeting is the forbidden outcome.

decisions_recorded.decision: in-repo surgical span rewriter; vendoring is the fallback
decisions_recorded.rationale: no comment-preserving JSONC editor exists offline; the repo already has the hard half of the scanner.

decisions_recorded.decision: new keys appended as the last member of their object
decisions_recorded.rationale: preserves human key order everywhere else; alphabetical insert would reorder the file on unrelated edits.

decisions_recorded.decision: base refresh by re-registration; fixed-base is the documented fallback
decisions_recorded.rationale: installSection is register+hooks and duplicate registration fails loud (measured at $H/dsh-settings/lib/index.js:327-331), so a second installSection call is impossible.

decisions_recorded.decision: TUI keeps a FALLBACK namespace registration, not a second owner
decisions_recorded.rationale: duplicate registration fails loud, but the section must not go 'unavailable' in a composition without the config plugin.

decisions_recorded.decision: the web card claims loopback-only persistence and the RENDERED card stays NOT-CLAIMED here
decisions_recorded.rationale: no browser exists in this environment, so 'the card renders / a click produces the mutate' is unverifiable and must not be asserted; only the protocol-level bridge and a static client-bundle assertion are witnessable.

decisions_recorded.decision: duplicate keys: edit the LAST occurrence, refuse on an ambiguous duplicated intermediate
decisions_recorded.rationale: JSON.parse is last-wins (measured), so editing the first occurrence would look successful and change nothing observable.

decisions_recorded.decision: N live roots REFUSE `ambiguous-multi-root` (candidate list named, no file written) instead of fanning out to all N — this REVERSES the first draft
decisions_recorded.rationale: t35 acceptance A3 requires the ambiguous multi-root path to warn and never silently write to a guessed path; N candidates mean the target cannot be PROVEN, and an unprovable target is refused exactly like an unprovable key span. Accepted cost, disclosed: with several live sessions a front-door edit persists to settings but not to a file until one workspace is live.

decisions_recorded.decision: mpd-config-plugin registers the `mpd` namespace (serving the file-derived base); mpd-tui-plugin becomes a pure consumer with a fallback registration only when the namespace is otherwise unserved
decisions_recorded.rationale: the namespace must serve the file-derived base, which only the module reading the files can supply; the TUI package still performs zero filesystem writes.

decisions_recorded.decision: the A6 negative-control hook is the row config key `writeBack: false` (default true), with env MPD_DSH_TUI_SETTINGS_BRIDGE=off as a secondary debugging lever; the switch disables ONLY the file write-back, never the namespace or precedence
decisions_recorded.rationale: a row key is composable from the lane's own patch layer, which is what a negative control needs; disabling the namespace too would make the control indistinguishable from an absent feature.

decisions_recorded.decision: a MISSING key path is INSERTED (never refused) and `span-not-proven` is reserved for genuinely unprovable shapes
decisions_recorded.rationale: the captain ruled insertion explicitly; otherwise a first-time key could never be written.
